slides.headline: 6 AI PROMPTS BLEW UP THIS WEEK AFTER A GUY USED ONE TO CUT HIS $1,200 HOSPITAL BILL TO $180
1) PASTE YOUR BILL AND LET AI FIGHT IT
slides.body: He pasted a $1,200 hospital bill into Claude. It dropped to $180. 'Here is my medical bill. Find every inflated charge, cite the correct rates, and write a formal dispute letter'

slides.headline: 2) RUN MOCK INTERVIEWS THAT PREDICT THE REAL THING
slides.body: He fed Claude the job listing. The interview felt like a rerun. He got hired. 'Here is the job description and my background. Interview me one question at a time, then critique my answers'

slides.headline: 3) SELL YOUR STUFF WHILE YOU SLEEP
slides.body: Pricing, listing, and haggling: one prompt handles all three. 'Here are photos of things I want to sell. Price each one fairly, write a marketplace listing for each, and draft replies to low offers'

slides.headline: 4) PREDICT EVERY QUESTION YOUR BOSS WILL ASK
slides.body: He ran this before every review. The real meeting felt scripted. 'You are a skeptical VP. Here is my presentation. List every question you'd ask and what would make each answer weak'

slides.headline: 5) REDESIGN ANY ROOM FROM ONE PHOTO
slides.body: She snapped one photo. Got a full redesign and a $500 shopping list. 'Here is my room. Redesign it like an interior designer and give me a shopping list to build it, under $500'

slides.headline: 6) AUDIT YOUR WORK BEFORE ANYONE ELSE DOES
slides.body: He split the finding from the judging. Weak claims got caught before clients saw them. 'Here is my draft. Flag every unsupported claim and list what I should verify before presenting'

slides.headline: SAVE THIS FOR WHEN YOU NEED THEM
slides.body: You'll want these prompts the next time you get a bill, a meeting, or a listing to write. We share these every week. Follow @yaffeai for daily AI news and real skills

caption:
Swipe for 6 AI prompts that went viral this week because people actually tested them and they worked 🔥

A bill-fighting prompt that cut $1,200 to $180, a mock interview prompt that made the real thing feel like a rerun, a marketplace prompt that prices and lists your stuff and handles the lowballers, a meeting prep prompt that predicts the exact questions your boss will ask, a room redesign prompt that rebuilds any space from one photo with a shopping list under $500, and a research audit prompt that catches every weak claim before anyone else reads it.

These aren't tricks. They're real prompts tested by thousands of people this week. The tools are free. The expensive version is the human expert who used to do the same job.
